dedupe_keys.name: issa innovative software for stability analysis of multi terminal hvdc hybrid ac dc multi energy grids

description: ISSA is a MATLAB tool for assessing the small-signal stability of hybrid AC/DC transmission systems, multi-terminal HVDC grids and converter-dominated multi-energy grids. It was published on Zenodo in April 2026 by Oriol Cartiel Arasa, Luis Sainz and Juan José Mesas, as part of a larger publication. It applies Resonance Mode Analysis to a dq-complex nodal admittance matrix evaluated over a user-defined frequency sweep, extracts modal properties by eigenanalysis, and judges stability with the Positive-Mode-Damping criterion. Numerical methods are chosen automatically, with a faster method for low-sparsity systems, a Lanczos method for general use and an Arnoldi method for very sparse large systems, and it has been tested on grids of up to 70,000 buses. Features include participation factors, analysis of up to ten dominant modes, oscillation propagation across the grid, an Excel input interface and automatic reports. Coverage is not tied to a place. The tool and a user tutorial are downloadable from Zenodo under CC BY 4.0 at no cost. Caveats: MATLAB is required, and the code is shipped as a RAR archive without a public repository. Simulation uses are screening converter-driven oscillation risks in AC/DC grids. Related records: model-odepower and model-power-system-small-signal-tool-manchester.
